draft.title: Reducing balance loans
card: On a reducing balance loan, interest is charged on the amount still owing. Each period, the interest is added and then the repayment M is taken off.
With balance B and rate r per period, the new balance is B × (1 + r) − M. Repeat this step for each period.
Example: $10 000 at 10% per year, repaid over 2 years. After year 1: 11 000 − M. After year 2: (11 000 − M) × 1.1 − M = 12 100 − 2.1M.
The loan is repaid when the balance after n periods is zero. Here 12 100 − 2.1M = 0, so M = 12 100 ÷ 2.1 = $5761.90 per year, to the nearest cent.
draft.remember: Balance each period = balance × (1 + r) − M. Set the final balance to zero to find M.

a.q: Ravi borrows $1000 at 5% per period. He makes a repayment of $300 at the end of the first period. What is the balance after that repayment?
a.why: Interest is added first: 1000 × 1.05 = 1050. Then the repayment comes off: 1050 − 300 = 750. $735 is wrong because it takes the repayment off before adding interest.
a.clue: Add the interest to the balance, then take off the repayment.

b.q: Lena borrows $2000 at 10% per year. She repays it with 2 equal repayments at the end of each year. What is each repayment, to the nearest cent?
b.why: After year 1 the balance is 2000 × 1.1 − M = 2200 − M. After year 2 it is 2420 − 2.1M. Setting this to zero gives M = 2420 ÷ 2.1 = $1152.38. $1210 is wrong because it halves 2420 and ignores that the first repayment cuts the interest in year 2.
b.clue: Write the balance after each year, then set the second one to zero.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's example, both questions and both explanations check out: 12 100 ÷ 2.1 = $5761.90, 1050 − 300 = $750, and 2420 ÷ 2.1 = $1152.38.
